#220243. Tech Report: Measles in America: Here's a constructive approach to beating the disease, based on Brazil's experience

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1386 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Measles in America: Here's a constructive approach to beating the disease, based on Brazil's experience

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1386 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Health experts saw it coming — the fact that after 26 years, the US would lose its status as measles-free.
  • On November 17, 2026, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) said the US had lost its measles elimination status, along with Mexico.
  • Look at Brazil, where in 2019, with more than 21,000 measles cases, the country also lost its measles-free status.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Health experts saw it coming — the fact that after 26 years, the US would lose its status as measles-free. Back in July 2026, DW reported how one epidemiologist had suggested an 'amnesia' about the measles risk was pushing a growth in US infections.

Four months later, it was official. On November 17, 2026, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) said the US had lost its measles elimination status, along with Mexico.

But it doesn't have to stay this way.

Look at Brazil, where in 2019, with more than 21,000 measles cases, the country also lost its measles-free status. But within five years — during the COVID-19 pandemic — it fought and won back its measles-free status. And since 2024, Brazil has stayed measles-free, even as the highly contagious disease spread across the rest of the Americas.

Sources indicate that in 2026, with the data available up to the time of writing this article, Brazil had only had 70 measles cases. They were all linked to infections brought in from abroad, often from neighboring Peru.

Sources indicate that brazil has fewer people than the US, about 213 million compared to the US's nearly 350 million, but the two countries are similar in size. So the comparison is worth considering.

Brazil moves fast. The PAHO asks countries to respond within 72 hours of a suspected measles case. Here's Brazil's own rule:.

Recent findings suggest that it has also made hunting for cases a national habit. In a program called "Dia S," health workers knock on doors and visit schools, daycare centers and churches to find people who may be sick but have not seen a doctor.

Brazil also holds mass vaccination days called "Dia D." There was one in November, in the area where Brazil borders Colombia and Peru.

If someone is diagnosed with measles, health workers try to track down every person the patient may have met ("contact persons") and vaccinate them and other people living nearby.

The country has so far provided more than 16 million doses of the measles vaccine in 2026 and has donated 500,000 doses to Peru.

Brazil isn't perfect, though. According to official estimates from the World Health Organization, only 76% of children got both required doses of the vaccine in 2025 — well short of the 95% target. Experts warn this leaves the country at risk because measles is so highly contagious. A country needs to be as close to 100% immunized as possible to protect people and stop the disease from spreading.

It has been revealed that "Elimination is not a trophy that we win once and put on a shelf. It must be protected every day," notes PAHO Director Jarbas Barbosa.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that the US lost its measles-free status because the PAHO found that the same strain of the virus had been spreading in the country for 12 months or more. Mexico and Bolivia lost their status on the same day as the US.

Industry observers note that the US has had more than 5,400 cases in 2026 (at time of writing), more than twice as many as in all of 2025, and about 19 times as many as in 2024. Nearly everyone who got sick with measles was unvaccinated or had an unknown vaccination status.

According to recent reports, US President Donald Trump signed an executive order on upcoming vaccination recommendations for children in August 2026. It came at a time, when, as we reported, experts said people had stopped getting vaccinated against measles because infection rates were low. But like PAHO's Barbosa said, neglecting vaccination when infection rates are low is a mistake.

It has been revealed that to be fair, Trump's executive order listed the measles vaccine in a top category of vaccinations recommended for every child. But the administration's stance on vaccination in general is unclear.

Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has often declared opposition to vaccination, including against measles, advising people to take vitamin A instead. In Texas, this led to children being hospitalized with toxic levels of the supplement, and left them with no protection against measles.

Before the COVID-19 pandemic, 95% of US kindergartners had their measles shots. Now, it's 92%, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Protection (CDC). That leaves about 280,000 kindergartners in the US unprotected.

In the Texas counties where a 2025 measles outbreak began, coverage was as low as 77% at the time.

US children usually need vaccines to start school, but most states let parents opt out for religious or personal reasons, with no doctor involved.

According to recent reports, but vaccination rates have fallen elsewhere in the world as well, including in Europe. In Germany, where measles infections have also risen, experts blame anti-vaccination rhetoric that emerged during the COVID-19 pandemic.

A person sick with measles can infect up to18 other, unprotected people. With vaccination, it is possible to increase the number of protected people and lower the number of people the sick person can infect.

To prevent a measles outbreak, a community needs about 95% of people to be vaccinated and/or immune. The vaccination consists of two doses of the MMR (measles, mumps, rubella) vaccine.

But even after the two doses, a person can expect to have only 97% protection against measles — 3% short of full protection — so, nearly everyone in the community has to be vaccinated to keep the average level of protect as close to 100% as possible.

"For some diseases like measles, even a small decrease in vaccination rates can lead to more outbreaks of disease [so] community immunity requires over 95% of susceptible individuals to be immunized," says Andrew Racine, president of the American Academy of Pediatrics.

Sources indicate that and the 95% has to hold everywhere. A good national average can be affected by, for example, a single school where only 70% of the children are vaccinated. And that is where the outbreak is likely to start.

Around the world, measles deaths have dropped by 88% since 2000, thanks to vaccines.

But progress has stalled. Only about three out of four children worldwide get both doses of the vaccine. The biggest outbreaks right now are in Bangladesh, Indonesia and Guatemala.

Industry observers note that data from Europe shows that things can get better. In the European Union, cases fell from more than 35,000 in 2024 to about 2,300 the following year, with no measles-related deaths.

Romania went from more than 30,000 cases in 2024 to about 4,200 in 2025.

In Hungary, where 99% of children are vaccinated, there have been no measles cases in the past year.

Recent findings suggest that but in January, six European countries lost their measles-free status, including the UK, Spain and Austria. Across Europe, eight out of ten people who got measles in 2025 were unvaccinated.

According to recent reports, the Americas are seeing a major surge in measles infections, with more than 58,000 cases in 2026, over four times as many as by November in 2025. Guatemala has been hit hardest, with almost 35,000 cases.

Recent findings suggest that the deadliest outbreaks are in Africa. African Union countries have so far reported nearly 1,800 measles deaths in 2026, about 1,650 of them in Democratic Republic of Congo. Yet, Sudan, despite the war, raised first-dose measles coverage by 22 percentage points in 2025, which was the world's largest gain.

Measles is extremely contagious. One person can infect up to 18 unprotected people, which makes it about 12 times more contagious than the flu.

The virus can linger in the air for up to two hours after a sick person has left the room. And people spread it before they know they are sick. Someone with measles is contagious for four days before the rash appears and four days after.

It's not just a rash. About one in five unvaccinated people who get measles in the US ends up in the hospital. Measles can weaken the immune system for years, making it harder to fight off other infections.

In a recent development, but it's preventable. Two doses of the MMR vaccine (which also protects against mumps and rubella) protect 97% of people for life.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sunday’s bruising 4-0 defeat at Anfield exposed the scale of the rebuild facing Mauricio Pochettino at Manchester United.

For all the scrutiny aimed at Man United’s midfield and attack, it is the fragility at the back that is of greatest concern - the club have now conceded more goals than any other side in Europe's top five leagues this season.

With the January transfer window fast approaching, Fulham’s Calvin Bassey - often linked with an Old Trafford move - is rapidly playing himself into contention for a switch.

It has been revealed that man United’s need for centre-half reinforcements could hardly be more urgent after the weekend's display. Matthijs de Ligt looked worryingly off the pace against Liverpool, struggling with his turning circle and repeatedly caught out whenever Andoni Iraola's side broke at speed.

Recent findings suggest that the long-term picture looks increasingly bleak, too. Lisandro Martinez is widely expected to move on at the end of the season after previously speaking out publicly against the club, leaving a left-footed vacancy at the heart of defence.

It has been revealed that across the rest of Pochettino’s central defensive options, there is a lack of ready-made solutions. Leny Yoro, who endured a miserable afternoon of his own on Merseyside, and Ayden Heaven are both still very junior in their development, while Harry Maguire isn't getting any younger.

Throwing teenagers and early-20-somethings into an Old Trafford pressure cooker every week is no recipe for climbing the table, nor can Man United rely indefinitely on an ageing veteran to bail them out, as Maguire has done so consistently in the past.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

That is why Bassey ticks so many boxes for Man United’s latest era under Pochettino.

Sources indicate that turning 27 on New Year’s Eve, the Nigeria international is entering his prime years as a defender. And having racked up more than 100 Premier League appearances since arriving in west London from Ajax in 2023, he brings the sort of battle-hardened top-flight pedigree Man United are crying out for.

In doing so, he removes the adaptation risk that has plagued so many overseas Old Trafford arrivals. His commanding display in Fulham’s 1-1 draw away at Manchester City on Saturday makes the appeal obvious; Bassey has good recovery pace, is dominant in physical duels, and comfortable defending wide channels.

Bassey won't cost the earth either as his initial four-year contract at Craven Cottage expires next summer, and although Fulham hold an option to extend his stay by a further 12 months, his contractual situation keeps any potential fee firmly within reach for a club of Man United's stature and commercial acumen.

Fulham are understandably eager to tie him down to fresh terms, but the lure of spearheading Pochettino’s Old Trafford reboot may prove hard to resist.

In FourFourTwo's view, if Bassey maintains his current level over the coming weeks, don't rule out a January approach.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ethan Nwaneri's Arsenal career appears to be floundering, with the on-loan Borussia Dortmund teenager facing a further transfer setback.

Nwaneri returns to his parent club tonight in the Champions League with the Bundesliga giants and is eligible to face Arsenal despite still being owned by the Gunners.

But beyond this campaign, his future remains uncertain, with manager Mikel Arteta even recently alluding to the teenager's struggles at Signal Iduna Park.

Nwaneri became the Premier League's youngest-ever player in 2022 at the age of 15 – with Max Dowman later taking that record – before establishing himself in the 2024/25 season as a serious option on the right wing for the Gunners.

But after going out on loan at Marseille last term and heading to Dortmund this time, the teenager is yet to impress, with Arteta even admitting this week that “moments are not enough” for Nwaneri in his development and that consistency must follow.

A report from Sport Witness, likewise, reads as bad news for the 19-year-old, with the Gunners now pursuing a move for Gilberto Mora as soon as January.

Mora was the youngest player selected for the 2026 World Cup and has impressed hugely in his native Mexico, courting the attention of virtually every major club in Europe.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

In attacking midfield areas, Arsenal already have the likes of Martin Odegaard, Mikel Merino, Eberechi Eze and Max Dowman – with the latter two options on the wing – and should Arsenal bring in another teenage talent, Nwaneri's first-team opportunities would appear even scarcer.

FourFourTwo understands that the Gunners were open to offers for the starlet over the summer, opting to retain him and develop him at one of the best finishing schools in European football, though the paths of Nwaneri and Hale End colleague Myles Lewis-Skelly have been drastically different, thanks, in part, due to competition for places.

With Liverpool also circling for Mora, however, the Gunners may well have to present a particularly enticing package to secure the 18-year-old.

According to the report, the youngster has a release clause of around €25 million, making any move for him particularly costly – and suggesting that the Gunners could well incorporate him into their first team immediately.

Industry observers note that nwaneri, meanwhile, is valued by Transfermarkt at €25m. Arsenal return to Champions League action tonight against Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium.

Xabi Alonso concedes Chelsea's defending has been nowhere near good enough – but the Blues boss believes his friend Jamie Carragher was wrong to brand Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana a 'massive problem' in his scathing analysis of the centre-back pairing.

Alonso claimed he had not seen Carragher's critique on Sky Sports' Monday Night Football after their 4-1 home loss to Leeds United.

When told his former Liverpool team-mate had remarked Colwill and Fofana 'will never work' as defensive partners and that Chelsea 'will never achieve anything' without fixing this problem, Alonso said: 'I must disagree. I disagree with Carra.

Recent findings suggest that 'For sure, you can have bad games. We were not good. But I've seen them play well, and I've seen them show good levels.

'This is the goal and the challenge – to be consistent in the performance and to be consistent in the basics and not to drop in certain games when we are facing a tough opponent. I understand it was not good enough.'.

Colwill and Fofana were bullied by Dominic Calvert-Lewin of Leeds, as they also were by Sunderland's Brian Brobbey. They will now face Liam Delap and Nottingham Forest on Friday night at a City Ground which will carry an intimidating atmosphere.

Xabi Alonso has hit back at former Liverpool team-mate Jamie Carragher after he labelled Chelsea's centre backs a massive problem.

Alonso and Carragher spent five seasons together as team-mates at Liverpool.

It has been revealed that alonso was strong in saying his side can have 'no excuses' for their slipping standards, having conceded 20 Premier League goals this season. 'When you have that feeling like we had on Saturday, it is not good,' the Chelsea manager stated.

'We have talked about what we can do better and what we have to do better. There are no excuses not to do better. There are things that we all can do, even if you have a bad day in terms of feeling something you have to do at this level.

In a recent development, 'The feeling of the last game is not good, but now it's about looking forward and showing a reaction. There are no excuses. There is no ifs, no buts. Just certainties and things we have to do.

According to recent reports, 'We can define on the training and the messaging. We need to show that, not just talk. Talk is cheap. It's about performing on the pitch.'.

In a recent development, john Terry works for Chelsea's academy part-time, assisting the youngsters coming through at Cobham. Terry is a club legend whose two strengths were defending and leadership.

Asked if he had thought about bringing him on to his staff, Alonso mentioned: 'We have talked because he's been around Cobham many times.

It has been revealed that 'He's working with the academy. We have people in the staff to prepare for that, and, for sure, the presence of John is always welcome.'.

Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana have endured poor starts to the season with Chelsea having already conceded 20 Premier League goals.

Sources indicate that pressed further on whether he had worked with the first team, Alonso added: 'This year? Not yet. But he's close to the team.'.

Meanwhile, Fofana has apologised to Chelsea for the unauthorised interview he conducted with a YouTuber which sparked a backlash from supporters online.

In it, the centre-back laughed off his penalty miss which condemned the club to their Carabao Cup exit at Liverpool, and revealed how his representatives advised him to honour his lucrative contract, worth £200,000 per week, when he was tempted to quit football amid his injury hell.

Industry observers note that alonso confirmed the club had spoken with Fofana and noted: 'He apologised. He knows it was not right, the moment, and it was not right, the content. We are here to take things seriously and he said that it's not going to be repeated.'.

When asked if Fofana had been fined, Alonso said: 'This is internal things.'.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • With World Cup and Olympic berths decided along the way, fans can watch all of the 2026 Concacaf W Championship on CBS Sports Golazo Network and Paramount+.
  • Here's everything you need to know about the upcoming tournament:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that just when you think you're going to settle in for a long winter's nap, there's more high-stakes women's soccer to watch. The 2026 Concacaf W Championship paves the way to the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup in Brazil and the 2028 Summer Olympics, and eight national teams from the region will play a knockout bracket starting Friday, Nov. 27.

With World Cup and Olympic berths decided along the way, fans can watch all of the 2026 Concacaf W Championship on CBS Sports Golazo Network and Paramount+.

Here's everything you need to know about the upcoming tournament:.

All times Eastern -- all games will air on Paramount+.

Friday, Nov. 27 (quarterfinals).

In a recent development, saturday, Nov. 28 (quarterfinals).

Industry observers note that saturday, Dec. 5 (third-place match and final).

The Concacaf W Championship is a senior women's national team championship tournament that doubles as the region's qualifier for both the World Cup and the Olympics.

This year's edition has a new format that sends teams to the 2027 World Cup and 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The biggest change is the quarterfinal bracket. The top two ranked teams, the United States and Canada, earned byes into the tournament. Jamaica, Costa Rica, Mexico, Panama, Haiti, and El Salvador all earned spots through the Concacaf W Qualifiers.

Back in 2022, eight finalists were placed into two groups of four, with the top two teams in each advancing into the semifinals and clinching World Cup spots. Third-place teams were given a chance to qualify in the inter-confederation playoffs. 2022 was also the first year the competition served as both a World Cup and Olympic qualifier, but only the champion and the winner of a two-leg playoff clinched Olympic berths.

Sources indicate that this year, the group stages are gone, and a single quarterfinal will decide who qualifies directly. In 2026, the quarterfinal winners all earn a place in the 2027 World Cup, and quarterfinal losers compete in a play-in round, with the two winners earning spots in the inter-confederation playoffs in February 2027.

It has been revealed that the two Concacaf W Championship finalists and the third-place finisher qualify for the 2028 Summer Games. The United States are hosts of the 2028 Olympics and qualify automatically, so if they finish in the top three, the fourth-place team takes the remaining Olympic spot.

The U.S. women's national team will face El Salvador for the first time in program history. El Salvador are the USWNT's first new opponent since playing Zambia in the Olympic group stage in July 2024.

The USWNT step into the competition as reigning Concacaf W Championship winners. They've won the last three tournaments and hold a record nine all-time titles. The USWNT won all five of their games in the 2022 W Championship without conceding a goal and outscored opponents 13-0. The USWNT are 106W-1D-0L in matches against teams ranked outside of FIFA's Top 25, drawing only to Costa Rica 0-0 in July 2024 in Washington, D.C.

In a recent development, manager Emma Hayes named a 23-player roster for the tournament, but recently made some changes following the 2026 NWSL Championship. Trinity Rodman, who sustained a shoulder injury, has been replaced by Jaedyn Shaw, and Shaw will be replaced by Lia Godfrey on the U-23 roster.

Kansas City Current defender Laney Rouse was also ruled out of the U-23 roster and is replaced by Denver Summit FC defender Natalie Means.

Industry observers note that el Salvador have never qualified for a Women's World Cup and will make their debut at the Concacaf W Championship. They qualified for the tournament by winning Group F with three clean sheets against Honduras, Barbados, and Trinidad & Tobago.

Head coach Eric Acuna is still leading the group after previous investigations into alleged abusive conduct,  and he publicly criticized players just last month after losses to Paraguay.

Players are trying to move forward and are led by Brenda Ceren, who led the team with five goals, followed by Danielle Fuentes with four, during the Concacaf W Qualifiers.

Italian sportswear giant Kappa has teamed up with streetwear label Cruel Pancake to unveil a one-off limited capsule collection titled Maestro of the Game â a nostalgic nod to the romance of 1990s and 2000s Italian football, fused with modern streetwear sensibilities.

The capsule consists of just four unisex pieces, each carrying strong retro football DNA.

In a recent development, leading the line is an oversized cream zip-up jacket with pink accents, a design that feels as though it was lifted straight from Serie A training grounds of the past. It is joined by a long-sleeved jersey with bold pink stripes, a co-branded logo, and âMaestro of the Gameâ emblazoned across the back.

A short-sleeved jersey follows, keeping things cleaner with white fabric and delicate pink pinstripes, while a pair of matching white-and-pink socks rounds off the set.

The Maestro of the Game collection is extremely limited, and will only be available for one day: October 4, via a pop-up at 118 Rue de Turenne, 75003 Paris. Visitors to the store will have the rare chance to pick up these exclusive pieces before they disappear.
